description: Catastrophic cloudburst over upstream catchment of Musi and Esi rivers. Water level at Afzalgunj bridge rose to 11 feet above roadway. Led to the historic flood mitigation design by Sir M. Visvesvaraya and construction of twin reservoirs Osman Sagar (1920) and Himayat Sagar (1927).
source_agency: Nizam's Public Works Department / Visvesvaraya Technical Committee Report (1909)
geographic_uncertainty: Historical municipal records; river stage benchmarked at Afzalgunj Bridge and Osmania General Hospital pillar.

provenance.source_title: Report on the Hyderabad Floods of 28th September 1908
provenance.publisher: H.E.H. The Nizam's Public Works Department (Committee chaired by Sir M. Visvesvaraya)
provenance.citation_detail: Visvesvaraya Technical Report (1909); 17.0 inches rainfall recorded at Shamshabad station; 425,000 cusecs computed at Afzalgunj.
provenance.evidence_note: Discharge of 12,034 m³/s (425,000 cusecs) is a post-hoc hydraulic slope-area estimate by Sir M. Visvesvaraya at Afzalgunj bridge, NOT a direct stream-gauge observation. Cited URL is a general state history page.
provenance.unresolved_issues: Primary manuscript tables from 1908 are preserved in state archives; exact page-level tables are not accessible via open web URL.

audit_trail.correction_rationale: Discharge reclassified from direct observation to hydraulic post-event estimate (slope-area method). Cited URL is a generic portal, not a primary data table.

description: Intense convective downpour concentrated over central and northern Hyderabad. Overwhelmed urban stormwater nalas and Hussain Sagar surplus weirs. Inundated over 70 low-lying colonies across GHMC.
source_agency: India Meteorological Department (IMD) / GHMC Flood Damage Assessment (2000)
geographic_uncertainty: Station measurement at Begumpet (17.442, 78.475); localized colony flooding varied based on micro-drainage.

provenance.source_title: IMD Monsoon Summary 2000 & Municipal Corporation of Hyderabad Damage Assessment Report
provenance.citation_detail: IMD Begumpet station 24h rainfall of 241.5 mm on 24 Aug 2000; MCH flood damage report documenting 70 flooded colonies.
provenance.evidence_note: 24h rainfall of 241.5 mm is verified from IMD historical precipitation records. Peak river discharge was previously reported as 1250 cumec, but no physical stream gauge existed to measure this flow; the number is an unsupported estimate and has been moved to audit trail.
provenance.unresolved_issues: Discharge was estimated without calibrated gauge; IMD URL is a regional landing page rather than a direct permanent report link.

audit_trail.correction_rationale: Peak river discharge of 1250.0 cumec stripped from observation field because no Musi stream-gauge telemetry existed in 2000; preserved in audit trail as unsupported estimate.

event_name: August 2008 Musi River Swell & Causeway Submergence
description: Continuous heavy monsoon rains in Ranga Reddy and Vikarabad catchments necessitated opening of 6 floodgates at Himayat Sagar and 4 gates at Osman Sagar. Moosarambagh and Chaderghat low-level causeways submerged for 36 hours.
source_agency: Government of Andhra Pradesh Irrigation Department / Hyderabad Traffic Police Advisories
geographic_uncertainty: Causeway submergence documented along 8 km riverine reach.

provenance.source_title: Irrigation Outflow Telemetry Bulletins & Traffic Police Causeway Advisories (August 2008)
provenance.publisher: Andhra Pradesh Irrigation Department & Hyderabad City Police
provenance.citation_detail: Traffic police advisories for Moosarambagh and Chaderghat closures; AP Irrigation Department gate release notices (6 gates Himayat Sagar, 4 gates Osman Sagar).
provenance.evidence_note: Peak discharge of ~480 m³/s (~17,000 cusecs) represents calculated reservoir gate outflow into Musi, NOT an open-channel stream-gauge measurement. Sourced agency was AP Irrigation Department (pre-Telangana bifurcation). Cited DES URL only contains annual totals.
provenance.unresolved_issues: Cited DES URL is a general department portal; 2008 daily gate logs are archived in physical state department ledgers.

audit_trail.correction_rationale: Downgraded confidence from HIGH to LOW; agency corrected to AP Irrigation Department; discharge reclassified as dam outflow estimate rather than stream observation.

description: Consecutive days of intense monsoon downpours caused breach of surplus nalas flowing into Alwal Cheruvu and Fox Sagar. Bhandari Layout in Nizampet remained submerged under 5 feet of stagnant water for 5 days.
rainfall_station: Hakimpet Air Force Station / TSDPS AWS
source_agency: GHMC Disaster Management / TSDPS Weather Bulletin (Sep 2016)
geographic_uncertainty: Northern urban lakes and chain nalas; municipal boundary Medchal/GHMC.

provenance.source_title: TSDPS Daily Rainfall Bulletin (September 2016) & GHMC Disaster Assessment
provenance.publisher: Telangana State Development Planning Society & GHMC
provenance.citation_detail: TSDPS Hakimpet AFS rainfall of 165.4 mm; Nizampet municipal flood damage logs.
provenance.evidence_note: Rainfall observed via TSDPS AWS at Hakimpet. Flooding occurred in Nizampet lake basins (Alwal and Fox Sagar nalas). Peak discharge of 210 cumec was previously asserted without stream gauge evidence; because this was a lake-chain breach outside the Musi mainstem, the discharge figure has been stripped and moved to audit trail.
provenance.unresolved_issues: Discharge was unsupported; TSDPS URL is a general portal; daily bulletin PDF requires manual portal search.

audit_trail.correction_rationale: Stripped unsupported 210 cumec river discharge. Flooding was caused by lake surplus nalas in Nizampet, not Musi River overflow.

description: Deep Depression BOB 02 made landfall and stalled over Telangana. Unprecedented 24h deluge broke 100-year records in eastern Hyderabad (320 mm at Ghatkesar, 288 mm at Hayathnagar). Osman Sagar and Himayat Sagar opened 14 and 8 gates respectively. Over 40,000 families displaced.
rainfall_station: TSDPS AWS Ghatkesar & IMD Begumpet (191.8 mm)
source_agency: TSDPS, IMD National Weather Summary, ISRO NRSC Bhuvan Flood Mapping (18 Oct 2020)
geographic_uncertainty: Satellite-mapped open-water inundation masks (Cartosat/Sentinel-1 SAR) combined with ground AWS telemetry.

provenance.source_title: ISRO / NRSC Bhuvan Satellite Flood Assessment & TSDPS Special Weather Bulletin (October 2020)
provenance.publisher: National Remote Sensing Centre (ISRO), TSDPS, and IMD
provenance.citation_detail: Bhuvan Sentinel-1 SAR and Cartosat flood inundation extent map (18 Oct 2020); TSDPS AWS Ghatkesar 320 mm 24h record; IMD Begumpet 191.8 mm record; Osman Sagar (14 gates) & Himayat Sagar (8 gates) release logs.
provenance.evidence_note: Precipitation and satellite inundation are verified from official TSDPS, IMD, and NRSC records. Peak river discharge of ~850 m³/s (~30,000 cusecs) represents combined dam gate outflow calculation, NOT a river stream-gauge observation. Copernicus GloFAS modelled reanalysis peak is 676.64 m³/s.
provenance.unresolved_issues: Satellite acquisition was captured on 18 Oct (4 days post-peak); river discharge is calculated dam outflow rather than physical stream telemetry.

audit_trail.correction_rationale: Downgraded confidence from VERY_HIGH to HIGH because river discharge is an outflow estimation rather than physical gauge telemetry and satellite scene was captured post-peak.

description: Short-duration cloudburst dumping 110 mm of rain within 2 hours during evening rush hour. Extensive waterlogging across core commercial districts and underpasses.
source_agency: GHMC Monsoon Emergency Action Cell / TSDPS Daily Rain Bulletin
geographic_uncertainty: Intense hyper-local cloudburst lasting 120 minutes; arterial road junction waterlogging.

provenance.source_title: TSDPS Hourly Rain Telemetry Bulletin (14 July 2021) & GHMC DRF Waterlogging Log
provenance.publisher: Telangana State Development Planning Society & GHMC
provenance.citation_detail: TSDPS Nampally AWS recorded 115.8 mm in 24 hours (110 mm in 2 hours); GHMC emergency reports for underpass waterlogging.
provenance.evidence_note: Rainfall verified from TSDPS AWS telemetry. Flooding was street-level stormwater stagnation; Musi River did not breach and no river-stage gauge recorded flow. Peak discharge of 95.0 cumec previously listed was an unsupported estimate and has been moved to audit trail.
provenance.unresolved_issues: River discharge was unsupported; event is hyper-local street waterlogging rather than river basin flood.

audit_trail.correction_rationale: Stripped unsupported discharge of 95.0 cumec. Event was short-duration urban stormwater surge with no river overflow.

description: Widespread monsoon depression over central India caused sustained inflow into Osman Sagar and Himayat Sagar. Continuous release of 8,000 cusecs into Musi River led to traffic closure on Chaderghat causeway and Moosarambagh bridge.
source_agency: Telangana State Disaster Management Authority (TG-SDMA) Alert Bulletin
geographic_uncertainty: Causeway closure enforced by Hyderabad Traffic Police; low-lying riverbank settlements evacuated.

provenance.source_title: TG-SDMA Flood Warning Bulletin & NDMA SACHET Alert Advisory (July 2022)
provenance.publisher: Telangana State Disaster Management Authority & NDMA
provenance.citation_detail: TG-SDMA alert bulletin ordering evacuation along Musi riverbank; Hyderabad Traffic Police closure of Moosarambagh causeway.
provenance.evidence_note: Official emergency alert verified via TG-SDMA / NDMA CAP protocol. Peak river discharge of 226.5 m³/s represents mathematical conversion of 8,000 cusecs released from Himayat Sagar gates, NOT an in-stream gauge observation.
provenance.unresolved_issues: Discharge is calculated dam outflow rather than continuous stage gauge measurement.

audit_trail.correction_rationale: Confidence adjusted from HIGH to MEDIUM to reflect that discharge is a reservoir gate release conversion rather than physical stream telemetry.

description: Successive waves of heavy monsoon showers caused waterlogging in 48 identified chronic water stagnation points across GHMC. Disaster Response Force (DRF) deployed for de-watering.
source_agency: GHMC DRF Operations Log & TSDPS Meteorological Data
geographic_uncertainty: Local street-level drainage bottlenecks along major transport corridors.

provenance.source_title: GHMC DRF Monsoon Incident Log & TSDPS Rainfall Report (July 2023)
provenance.publisher: GHMC & Telangana State Development Planning Society
provenance.citation_detail: TSDPS AWS Shaikpet recorded 128.5 mm; GHMC DRF logged 48 chronic waterlogging de-watering deployments.
provenance.evidence_note: Precipitation verified from TSDPS AWS telemetry. Flooding was localized street waterlogging along road underpasses and arterial corridors. Discharge value of 85.0 cumec previously reported was unsupported and has been moved to audit trail.
provenance.unresolved_issues: Discharge unsupported; drainage bottleneck event without riverbank overflow.

audit_trail.correction_rationale: Stripped unsupported discharge of 85.0 cumec. Event was urban transport bottleneck waterlogging without river gauge records.
